note: Shared golden spec for math tokenization parity between the published renderer and conservative line-based editor scanners. Byte-identical copies live in each consumer repo; bump `version` and update every copy together when semantics change. `published` and `editor` list the ordered math renderings for the input (empty = the source stays literal text; kinds: display | inline | error). Cases where the columns differ are known, deliberate divergences — changing either column is a semantic change that must be conscious. `editorGate` marks cases the editor rejects via a non-scanner gate (e.g. code spans), so scanner-only harnesses skip the editor assertion.

cases.name: mid-paragraph-double-dollar
cases.note: known divergence: the renderer keeps remark-math's inline reading; the editor leaves a $$..$$ raw unless it owns its lines

cases.name: own-line-inside-paragraph
cases.note: known divergence: promotion only rewrites whole paragraphs; the editor's line scanner renders any standalone $$..$$ line

cases.name: blockquote-display
cases.note: known divergence: the blockquote marker keeps the line from being standalone for the editor; the renderer keeps the inline reading

cases.name: unterminated-display
cases.note: known divergence: remark-math's flow form treats `$$x` as an unterminated fence and emits an empty display block; the editor keeps unterminated $$ raw

cases.name: unfenced-multiline-display
cases.note: known divergence: remark-math's flow form eats `$$a` as a fence opening and garbles the rest; prefer the fenced $$\n..\n$$ shape

cases.name: multiline-inline
cases.note: known divergence: remark-math allows single-$ spans across a soft break; the editor's inline scanner is single-line
